questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

Which situation should not lead to market failure?

options.A: Managers in a firm have information unavailable to shareholders.
options.B: Resources such as solar energy can be continuously renewed.
options.C: Resource allocation is not always Pareto efficient.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows a customer’s budget line for two goods, X and Y. Y Y O X X Assuming the price of X does not change, the slope of the budget line will become steeper when:

options.A: the consumer’s income falls.
options.B: the consumer’s income rises.
options.C: the price of Y falls.

questions.questionText: A consumer maximises his utility by spending all his income on goods X and Y. New research reveals that good X is a merit good providing the consumer with more utility than was previously realised. The consumer’s income and the prices of goods X and Y are unchanged. If the consumer behaves rationally, how will he respond to the findings of the research? quantity of quantity of good X purchased good Y purchased

options.A: decreases increases
options.B: increases decreases
options.C: increases unchanged

questions.questionText: Two manufacturing firms in the same industry, producing similar products, are considering merging together. What would be the least convincing reason for merging?

options.A: It would enable greater bargaining power when buying raw materials.
options.B: It would enable technical economies of scale.
options.C: It would produce savings in management and administration costs.
options.D: It would reduce the dependence of the firms on the suppliers of raw materials.

questions.questionText: The following schedule gives information about a firm’s costs. total variable costs $6400 average fixed costs $20 average total costs $100 Which output would be consistent with these costs?

options.A: 32 units B 50 units C 64 units D 80 units

questions.questionText: Which objective involves the managers of a firm operating with just enough profit to keep shareholders happy whilst maintaining sales revenue above its profit-maximising level?

options.A: achieving below normal profit
options.B: maximising the quality of the output
options.C: profit satisficing

questions.questionText: Which measure to reduce the abuse of monopoly power is an example of regulation?

options.A: legislation to forbid price fixing by cartels
options.B: removal of import tariffs
options.C: subsidising small firms

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a Lorenz curve, with two areas, X and Y, identified. cumulative line of % of income perfect equality X Y Lorenz curve cumulative % of households How is the corresponding Gini coefficient calculated?

options.A: X divided by (X plus Y)
options.B: (X plus Y) divided by X
options.C: (X plus Y) divided by Y

questions.questionText: Which combination of government policies will be most likely to affect inter-generational equity?

options.A: a fall in overseas aid expenditure and a rise in domestic military spending
options.B: a fall in the top rate of income tax and a rise in the sales tax (VAT) on luxury goods
options.C: a rise in educational maintenance allowances and a fall in state pensions
options.D: a rise in unemployment benefits and a rise in national insurance contributions

Labour is the only variable factor of a profit-maximising firm which is a price-taker in the labour market. From what is the firm’s demand curve for labour derived?

options.A: its marginal factor cost curve
options.B: its marginal revenue curve
options.C: its marginal revenue product of labour curve

questions.questionText: A developing country receiving foreign financial aid is most likely to experience economic growth in the long run if it uses the money to:

options.A: boost welfare benefits for the poorest households.
options.B: pay for imports of capital goods.
options.C: reduce environmental pollution.
options.D: reduce income tax for all households.

questions.questionText: The Multidimensional Poverty Index uses benchmarks to measure the severity of poverty. Which country suffers most from deprivation in health and living standards compared with deprivation of education? deprivation contribution to overall poverty (%) country living education health standards

options.A: Bangladesh 28.4 26.1 45.5
options.B: Burkino Faso 39.0 22.5 38.5

questions.questionText: Which is the most accurate statement about developing economies?

options.A: A possible dependency on primary products for export revenues means that developing economies are reliant on the industrialised world for manufactured products.
options.B: High levels of capital per head mean that developing economies must rely on overseas trade if they are to achieve higher growth rates.
options.C: High real GDP per head, plus high rates of population growth, reduce the ability of developing economies to increase their standard of living.
options.D: Migration of labour from rural to urban areas is of significance only if it results in labour shortages in the rural economy.

questions.questionText: A benefit of foreign direct investment (FDI) is better training for local workers leading to improved human capital and large productivity increases.

options.A: shift left shift left
options.B: shift right shift left
options.C: shift left shift right

questions.questionText: A director becomes redundant as the result of a company merger. His salary was $80000. In his first year after redundancy he earns $60000 in consultancy fees, $10000 in dividends on shares, and saves $8000 by dismissing his gardener. What is the resulting change in measured national income in the first year?
What reduces the value of the multiplier?

options.A: an increase in government investment expenditure
options.B: an increase in consumption
options.C: an increase in the rate of taxation
options.D: an increase in the volume of exports

options.A: the balance of payments position

options.D: the standard of living in the country

questions.questionText: Which condition for macroeconomic equilibrium is correct?

options.A: G – T = S + I + X – M
options.B: I – S = G – T + M – X
options.C: M – X = I – S + G – T
options.D: X – M + G = S + I – T

questions.questionText: What describes a Keynesian measure to reduce cyclical unemployment?

options.A: adopting a supply-side policy to retrain unskilled workers
options.B: allowing the private sector to take over the supply of merit goods
options.C: increasing the ratio of capital equipment to manual labour in production
options.D: using fiscal policy to increase effective demand

questions.questionText: An economy imports most of the factors of production used in the manufacture of its exported goods. What effect would depreciation of this economy’s rate of exchange have? price of imported price of exported goods in the goods in the domestic currency domestic currency

options.A: fall fall
options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall

options.A: an increase in government expenditure on goods and services
options.B: an increase in government expenditure on training schemes to address skill shortages
options.C: an increase in the period when the unemployed are eligible for welfare benefits
